newsitem.title: USA: Stocks jump as economic numbers ease rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Stocks jump as economic numbers ease rate hike fears.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks soared Tuesday as a new batch of economic numbers eased fears that the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates again to head off inflationary pressures.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 105.16 points at 6,888.18 after rising as high as 6,897.41, or just below the key technical resistance of 6,900.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 8 to 2 on active volume of 314 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The rally was just as explosive in the inflation-sensitive bond market, where the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond gained more than a full point, sending its yield down to 7.01 percent from Monday's 7.11 percent. Last Friday the yield was at 7.14 percent.
"The rally is nice and broad and not giving anyone a chance to buy on the dips. There aren't any," said Bill Meehan, an analyst at Prudential Securities.
"I don't know if this precludes Fed action, but it puts a big dent in the case for aggressive imminent multiple moves. That's what the market is celebrating," he said.
In late March, the Fed raised short-term interest rates for the first time in more than two years.
The quarter-percentage-point increase by the central bank boosted borrowing costs, and helped trigger a market correction that pulled the Dow from a record high of 7,085.16 on March 11.
The new data on the economy lessened concern about another rate hike.

"The market was set up for the worst," Meehan said. "The choppiness we have been seeing indicated as much. But this is as good as it gets, and it may take any sting out the (April) jobs report on Friday. The glass was half full, then half empty. Now it's half full again."
Wall Street was celebrating news that the Employment Cost Index in the first quarter inched up only 0.6 percent, which was well below the 0.9 percent gain expected by Wall Street.
Also helping sentiment was an unexpected drop of 3.0 percent in durable goods orders in March, the largest drop since August 1996.

The economic reports were welcome news, as they indicated the economy's growth may be slowing and inflation is still in check -- which should lessen the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again at its May 20 policy-setting meeting.

"I don't think the economy just got bad in the last week," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter. "It does slow the Fed's agenda. But the Fed has to wait and see if the trend is changing or if this is a blip."
Boosting the Dow, was a rally in International Business Machines Corp., which said it was raising its dividend, splitting its stock and increasing its stock buyback. IBM was up 5-1/8 at 155-1/2.
Technology stocks were also doing well, boosting the Nasdaq Composite Index by 20.11 points to 1,237.14.
Cisco Systems Inc. was up 2 at 48-1/2, Intel Corp. gained 2-7/8 at 149-1/8, Microsoft Corp. was up 3-3/8 at 118-1/4 and Ascend Communications Inc. rose 2-3/8 to 53-1/4.
"You have seen the bottoms in a number of key groups like the semiconductors and possibly even in the networking equipment issues," Canelo said.
Meehan said financial stocks were among the immediate beneficiaries of stability in the bond market.
"This is one of the top sectors, and we think investors should focus on it. It's had some nice pullbacks," he said.
Among individual banks, Citicorp was up 5-1/8 at 112-3/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp. was up 3-3/8 at 90-7/8.
Bucking the trend were tobacco companies. Philip Morris Cos. was down 1-3/4 at 37-7/8 and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. fell 1-3/4 to 27-1/8.
